subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — Atlas Payments (pilot sizing & next steps)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — Atlas Payments

Thanks again for taking the call earlier, Sara — appreciate the time. I wanted to capture a concise recap so we all have the same picture and clear next steps. Please correct me where I’ve misread anything.

Key pain points you shared
- Settlement & reconciliation spikes: periodic batch jobs (02:00 UTC) produce large inference fanout that pushes your current endpoint latency into the 2–3s range and increases failed authorizations.
- PCI scope / data isolation: infra team needs isolation for inference serving (no shared-tenancy on GPUs) and proof of encryption at rest.
- Predictable throughput for peak windows: you need a capacity profile you can rely on during settlement and promo spikes.

Current stack (as you told us)
- Production traffic routed through an internal proxy to an on-prem inference cluster (mixed GPU fleet)
- Model: a distilled LLM serving token classification & light generation (avg prompt+response ~350 tokens)
- Auth flow: synchronous call path for each transaction (P95 target currently missed)

Success criteria for a pilot / evaluation
1) Achieve P95 latency < 150 ms for auth checks during baseline traffic (30% sample)
2) Support sustained 2,000 TPS for 10m window during settlement with a 3x burst headroom for 30m without degraded P95 beyond 300 ms
3) Isolation: reserved pool (no multi-tenant co-location) and KMS integration for model keys

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to produce an initial sizing estimate for a reserved GPU pool (ballpark in this thread). Laura and Karthik will draft capacity options and a cost delta.
- Atlas to share a small traffic trace (anonymized) or the CSV you mentioned so we can tune batch sizes and KV cache expectations (Sara / Peter).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Atlas infra (network, KMS, VPC/VLAN) — suggested week of Dec 6.
- Draft a pilot SOW (attached v1) that covers 4–6 weeks of reserved pool testing, metrics, and rollback criteria.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pilot-sow-v1.pdf (pilot SOW stub)

Open questions for Atlas (short list)
- Confirm average tokens per auth request (you mentioned ~350 combined, please confirm distribution).
- Can infra provide egress/IP allowlist constraints and whether a site-to-site VPN is preferred vs. VPC peering?
- Any compliance checklist items beyond PCI that we should add up front?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive once we have your preferred contacts and a preferred date range.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@atlaspay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — Atlas Payments

Thanks Marcus — this looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The 2,000 TPS target is accurate for our settlement batch at peak; sustained for ~8–12 minutes is common.
- Token distribution: median ~220 tokens, 95th ~540 tokens (includes prompt + response). I’ll attach a sanitized CSV of a week of traffic slices for the Nov 18–24 window.
- Compliance: PCI is the main gating item; we also need evidence of key lifecycle management (rotation logs) for any customer-managed keys. SOC2 is helpful but not mandatory for the pilot.

Looping in Peter Chang (infra) who will own the network/KMS questions: peter.chang@atlaspay.com

We’re generally supportive of a December pilot. Preferred weeks: Dec 6–10 or Dec 13–17.

Attachments: atlas-capacity-report-nov2026.csv

—
Sara Wong
Head of Product — Risk & Authorization | Atlas Payments
sara.wong@atlaspay.com

From: Peter Chang <peter.chang@atlaspay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sara Wong <sara.wong@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 00:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — Atlas Payments

Thanks for the summary. A few infra-specific items we need clarified before the tech deep-dive:
1) Network: Do you support IP allowlisting for a reserved cluster and can you accept a list of /32s for our outbound egress? Any preference for site-to-site VPN vs. VPC peering?
2) KMS: We require BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with rotation logs and an HSM-backed option. Can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS & customer-provided CMKs?
3) Storage & models: Are models encrypted at rest in your private deployment, and what SLAs exist around model artifact retention?
4) Observability: We need token-level latency breakdowns and per-request trace ids to tie back to our logs (no sampling for auth flows).

Also: can you share a rough GPU-equivalent sizing for the 2,000 TPS baseline + 3x burst so we can validate against rack/cab space and power?

Peter Chang
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Atlas Payments
peter.chang@atlaspay.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Peter Chang <peter.chang@atlaspay.com>, Sara Wong <sara.wong@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 02:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — Atlas Payments

Peter — great questions. Quick answers below; Laura & Karthik, please add if I missed anything (and we’ll include detail in the deep-dive slides).

Network & connectivity
- IP allowlist: yes — we support /32 allowlists. Both site-to-site VPN and VPC peering are supported; preference usually driven by customer egress rules. We’ll capture MTU/throughput expectations during the tech call.

KMS / keys
- BYOK: supported. We can integrate with AWS KMS and accept customer-managed CMKs; HSM-backed keys are supported via our KMS provider integrations. Rotation logs and audit evidence can be provided as part of the Private deployment package.

Storage & model artifacts
- Models are encrypted at rest by default in Private deployments. Retention is configurable; for pilot we typically keep artifacts for 90 days unless longer retention is requested.

Observability
- We’ll surface token-level latency breakdowns and will instrument per-request trace ids for auth flows (we recommend no sampling for those routes). Redwood Console will provide per-route P95/P99 and token counts.

Sizing (ballpark)
- Initial conservative estimate for 2,000 TPS baseline (auth flow, mixed 220–540 tokens): ~4 x A100-equivalent GPUs sustained.
- To support 3x burst (6,000 TPS) for short windows, we recommend either burst capacity on top of the reserved pool (2x additional GPUs as burst) or a reserved pool sized to 6 GPUs if you prefer headroom without burst orchestration.
- Laura / Karthik will produce a short matrix with cost + expected latencies per option.

Next steps (action items)
- Laura: produce pool-sizing calc + two commercial options (reserved4 + burst vs reserved6) by Mon Nov 29.
- Karthik: prepare the tech-deep-dive slide deck (network/KMS checklist + observability plan).
- Atlas: share the sanitized CSV (Sara) and confirm preferred week for the deep-dive (Dec 6–10 or Dec 13–17).
- I’ll circulate a proposed calendar invite after we lock a date.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pilot-sow-v1.pdf

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Internal note to Laura & Karthik (inline): please keep the sizing conservative — Atlas will value predictability and isolation. Include a short runbook for rollback criteria in the SOW.
